key_safety.text: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, occurred in 3 of 106 (3%) treated patients; signs/symptoms consistent with or possibly related to hypersensitivity occurred in 21 of 106 (20%). Most common adverse reactions in infants with rapidly progressive LAL deficiency (occurring in >30% of patients) included diarrhea 6 (67%), vomiting 6 (67%), fever 5 (56%) and rhinitis 5 (56%); in pediatric/adult patients the most common included headache 10 (28%) vs placebo 6 (20%) and fever 9 (25%) vs placebo 7 (23%).

citations.quote: In clinical trials, 3 of 106 (3%) patients treated with KANUMA experienced signs and symptoms consistent with anaphylaxis.

In clinical trials, 21 of 106 (20%) KANUMA-treated patients, including 9 of 14 (64%) infants and 12 of 92 (13%) pediatric patients, 4 years and older, and adults, experienced signs and symptoms either consistent with or that may be related to a hypersensitivity reaction.
